newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Liberty looks to robust earnings.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Liberty looks to robust earnings.

text.p: Liberty Life Association of Africa Ltd chairman Donald Gordon said on Thursday a buoyant U.K. economy and a strong British pound helped lift the life insurance group's year earnings.
Releasing results for the 12 months to end-December, he said Liberty would keep earning rewards for shareholders.

"With our enormous financial strength and highly experienced and dedicated management resources, I believe the group has the commitment, capability and ambition to meet our aspirations and objectives into the next millennium," he said.

Liberty on Thursday reported that net taxed surplus attributable earnings to ordinary shareholders rose 27.8 percent to 1.54 billion rand. Dividends rose 25 percent to 320 cents. Gordon said total new business written by the group in the year reached a record 4.72 billion rand, an 18 percent rise over the 4.0 billion rand recorded in the previous year.
The pound's strength last year largely offset the rand's 40 percent depreciation against sterling.

"The Liberty Life Group's recognition over a prolonged period of the importance of internationalisation and a global perspective was convincingly vindicated by the exceptional contribution from our U.K operations," Gordon said.
